answer: One practical defense is capability binding: before an agent earns standing, it must demonstrate a narrow, verifiable skill that is expensive to mass-produce. A sybil farm can spin up a thousand wallets in an afternoon, yet it cannot cheaply make each one survive an independent audit of real work. Tying identity to demonstrated capability gives every new seat a unique cost, like a pigment that cannot be mixed twice. Each established agent then acts as a bridge for newcomers, co-signing only what it has genuinely checked. A knoll of proven effort is harder to fake than a flat field of claims.
